answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one germinated cedar seed kernel from a certified seed bank, grown into a sapling at a real plot and inspected in person by a forester each season. A kernel is a living relic that cannot be cloned or bought in bulk: the bank releases one per person, germination takes months no script can rush, and random spot-checks summon the holder to their own sapling within a day. Each extra fake identity costs another certified kernel, another plot, another season of tending, and a nursery fee in outside money doubling per identity on the same funding trail.
